title: How to Make a TikTok Ad for Your Store | AIVideosUGC
description: Make your first TikTok ad from one product photo: pick one reason to buy, show the product in action, post a vertical 9:16 video, launch on a small budget.
h1: How to Make a TikTok Ad When You've Never Made One
lead: To make a TikTok ad, pick one product and one reason to buy, start with that product in action, and post a vertical clip on a budget you can pause.
summary: One reason to buy, a vertical clip that starts with the product in action, then your own line and a licensed track, then a small first campaign.

sections.h2: How should TikTok ads for small business start?
paras: Choose one product and finish this sentence: people buy this because it does one specific thing.

"A phone stand that folds flat enough for a jacket pocket" can be shown. "High quality and stylish" cannot. A candle that burns down to the glass, a leash clip that opens with one hand, or a lid that does not leak when tipped: each one points to a scene. One reason is enough for a first ad.
sections.alt: Adult woman applies cream from a plain light-peach tube to her cheek at the seaside.

sections.h2: What TikTok video ad tips matter in the first two seconds?
paras: Show the product doing something immediately. Skip logo cards and slow fades.
A hand snapping a stand open, a drink poured over ice, or a shoe turning to show the sole gives people a reason to stop. If the product is still off screen when someone scrolls past, they are gone.
sections.alt: Two adult hands spread white cream from a plain peach tube across the back of a hand.

sections.h2: How do I make a vertical video ad for products from one photo?
paras: Upload a clear product photo, describe one action in a single sentence, and choose the tall 9:16 frame.

"A hand unfolds a slim black phone stand on a cafe table and sets a phone in it, soft daylight" is a complete request. Leave prices and headlines out of that sentence. [AI image to video](page:image-to-video) and [URL to video](page:url-to-video) are other ways to start a clip. [AI product video generator](page:product-videos) fits when you want a short demo rather than an ad opening. Any person on screen is generated. Do not present them as a customer.
sections.alt: Adult hands hold a plain peach sunscreen tube over a blank notebook on a bright cafe table.

sections.h2: How long should the first TikTok ad be?
paras: Pick 6, 10, 15, or 30 seconds based on how much the product needs to do.

Six seconds fits one motion, such as a stand snapping open. Ten seconds fits a short demo. Fifteen seconds fits a simple sequence. Thirty seconds fits a longer one. Those lengths cost 24, 40, 60, and 120 credits. The cost shows before the job starts, and a failed job returns the credits. Each run makes one clip, so a second opening is another job, not another shoot.
sections.alt: Adult hands turn one plain peach sunscreen tube for a pre-launch check.

sections.h2: How do I add captions and sound after the download?
paras: Add the line, the price, and the sound in TikTok's editor or CapCut. Captions are not added for you.

Keep words in the middle of the frame. The account name, caption, and buttons sit along the bottom and the right edge. For the track, use TikTok's Commercial Music Library or another source cleared for ads. A song that is fine on a personal post is often not cleared for advertising.
sections.alt: One adult hand smooths white cream along a forearm beside a plain peach tube.

sections.h2: How do I launch a first TikTok ad campaign?
paras: Send people to the product page for the item in the clip, set a daily budget you can afford while you learn, and let it run for a few days before you judge it.

Write the caption the way you would text a friend: one line, no pile of hashtags. Watch it once on mute and once with sound. The product should be on screen in the first two seconds, the words should be readable, and the price in the ad should match checkout. If you made two openings, run them together, with the same audience and the same budget.
sections.alt: Adult hands hold a plain peach sunscreen tube beside a notebook on a bright desk.

paras: One product, one reason, a 9:16 clip that starts with the action, then your own line and a licensed track.
Credits are 24, 40, 60, or 120 for 6, 10, 15, or 30 seconds. Start with a budget you can pause, and read the first few days before you spend more.

faq.q: What size should my first TikTok ad be?
faq.a: Use 9:16 so the clip fills the phone. Keep the product and any words you add away from the bottom and the right edge, where the app's own buttons sit.

faq.q: Do I need to film a creator?
faq.a: No. Start from a product photo and a sentence about the action. If a person appears, they are generated. Do not name them as a buyer or a reviewer.

faq.q: Does the clip come with captions?
faq.a: No. Add captions, the price, and music after you download, in TikTok or CapCut, so the spelling and the track license stay under your control.

faq.q: How many credits does a 15-second ad use?
faq.a: A 15-second clip uses 60 credits. Six seconds is 24, ten is 40, and thirty is 120. A failed job returns the credits.

faq.q: What if the product in the clip does not match my page?
faq.a: Do not launch that file. Make it again from a sharper photo or a plainer sentence, and check color, version, and price against the page you will send people to.

faq.q: How long should I wait before changing the ad?
faq.a: Give it a few days. Look at how many people stay past the opening, how many click, and what a sale costs. A single afternoon is too short to call a winner.

cta_lead: Turn one product photo into a 9:16 clip, add your offer in TikTok or CapCut, and launch on a budget you can pause.
